title: Rinchenpong and Kaluk: where to stay, what to see
meta_description: Rinchenpong or Kaluk? Where to stay on the ridge at every budget, the 1730 monastery, Resum Gompa, Poison Lake and the best Kangchenjunga viewpoints.
summary: Rinchenpong and Kaluk are twin villages about 3 km apart on a ridge at roughly 1,700 m, facing Kangchenjunga. Stay in Rinchenpong to walk to the old monastery and Resum Gompa; stay in Kaluk for village resorts and wide views. Two nights is right. Homestays start around ₹1,200 per person with meals.

sections.heading: Two villages, one ridge
paras: Rinchenpong and Kaluk sit on the same forested ridge in Soreng district, at about 1,700 m, roughly 40 km and two hours above Jorethang and about 125 km from NJP. Until the district was created in December 2021 they were part of West Sikkim, and many maps and booking sites still say so. Pelling is about 35–40 km away, 1.5–2 hours by road, which makes the pair an easy add-on to a West Sikkim trip.

The reason to come is the view. From almost every terrace on the ridge the Kangchenjunga range stands across the valleys to the north, with Kabru, Rathong and Pandim in the line. Sunrise turns the snow pink, and from October to March the mountains are usually out for most of the morning. The rest is quiet: forest walks, two old monasteries, cardamom and orange orchards, and evenings with very little traffic.

Kaluk is the larger settlement, with a small bazaar, schools and several resorts. Rinchenpong is more scattered and climbs higher towards the monastery. You can walk between them in under an hour, so wherever you sleep, you can see both.

sections.heading: What to see in Rinchenpong
paras: Rinchenpong Monastery stands above the village at a little over 1,700 m. Wikipedia, citing local records, dates it to 1730 and names its founder as Ngadakpa Lama, which would make it one of the older monasteries in Sikkim. Its best-known image is the Ati Buddha (Adi-Buddha, the primordial Buddha) shown in the yab-yum posture, blue and in union with a female figure, which is unusual for Sikkim. Ask the caretaker before entering the shrine room, and dress modestly.

Above the monastery a forest trail climbs to Resum Gompa, a small monastery on the crest of the ridge. The walk takes about 30–45 minutes each way through oak and rhododendron, and the view from the top looks both north to the snow peaks and south across the Rangeet valley.

Below the village is a small pond known as Bikh Pokhari, the Poison Lake. As told locally and repeated on Wikipedia, defenders poisoned its water during a fight with British troops in the 19th century to stop them advancing. The written sources for this are thin, so treat it as a village story rather than recorded history. There is also a patch of forest named Rabindra Smriti Van; as told locally, Rabindranath Tagore stayed in the area, though we have not found a written source to confirm it.

sections.heading: What to see in Kaluk
paras: Kaluk is described on Wikipedia as one of the windiest places in Sikkim, and afternoons on the ridge can be brisk even in spring. Its main sights are the views. Megi Dara, a hilltop with a newer monastery and a reserve forest, is the favourite sunrise point, and the Durga Mandir is a local landmark. The roads between Kaluk and Rinchenpong pass through orange and cardamom orchards and small farms growing maize, ginger and vegetables.
From Kaluk you can also drive down to the Rangeet river for a change of scene, or out along the ridge towards Hee Bermiok and Dentam, which belong to Gyalshing district.

sections.heading: Where to stay at every budget
paras: Both villages have homestays, small hotels and a handful of village resorts. The properties below are real and were operating at our last check; prices are indicative 2026 bands and change by season, so check current status before you travel. Avoid the October and December holiday weeks unless booked early.

sections.heading: Rinchenpong or Kaluk: how to choose
paras: Choose Rinchenpong if you want to walk. The monastery, Resum Gompa and Poison Lake are all on foot from the village, and the homestays here are close to the forest. Yangsum Heritage Farm, an old family farmhouse set in its own fields, is the ridge's most characterful place to stay and suits couples and anyone who likes food grown on the farm.

Choose Kaluk if you want a resort with a garden, a bigger room and a view from your bed. Kaluk is also better if you are travelling with older parents, as the resorts are on the road and need less climbing. Families on a budget do well in Kaluk homestays, which are cheaper than the resorts but share the same view.

Whichever village you pick, ask for a north-facing room: the mountain view is the point of being here, and a room facing the road or the hillside behind costs nearly the same. In April and May, when haze is common, a room with a balcony lets you catch the brief clear spells at dawn without getting dressed.
list: Couples: Yangsum Heritage Farm or a Kaluk resort with a mountain-facing room
Families: a Kaluk resort or a large homestay on the road
Solo and backpackers: Zostel Rinchenpong or a family homestay
Seniors: Kaluk, on the motor road, ground-floor room
Birders and walkers: a Rinchenpong homestay near the monastery trail

sections.heading: A simple two-day plan
paras: This is the plan we give most guests who arrive from NJP on day one and leave on day three. It needs no car once you are on the ridge, apart from the short hop to Megi Dara, which you can also walk if you start early.

On the first evening, after the 5–6 hour drive, do nothing more than find a terrace and watch the light go off the snow peaks. Dinner in the homestay is usually at about 7 pm, and nights are cool enough for a jacket in every month except June to August.

The full day starts before dawn. From October to March the sun reaches Kangchenjunga at around 5:30–6:15 am, and the first fifteen minutes are the best. After breakfast, walk up to Rinchenpong Monastery, then continue on the forest trail to Resum Gompa and back. In the afternoon, stroll down past Poison Lake and over to Kaluk through the orchards, have tea in the bazaar, and come back by shared jeep or on foot. On the last morning, take a second sunrise from Megi Dara before the long drive down.
list: Day 1: arrive from NJP, evening on the terrace
Day 2 morning: sunrise, monastery, Resum Gompa walk
Day 2 afternoon: Poison Lake, orchards, Kaluk bazaar
Day 3: Megi Dara sunrise, drive to NJP or on to Pelling

sections.heading: How long to stay and getting there
paras: Two nights is the right length: one full day for the monastery, Resum Gompa and Kaluk, and two sunrises in case one is cloudy. Add a third night if you want a day trip to Hilley for the Barsey rhododendron walk (about 2–2.5 hours each way by car) or simply want to do nothing.

From NJP or Bagdogra the drive takes 5–6 hours via Melli and Jorethang. The first stretch uses NH10, which closes after landslides in the monsoon; drivers then come round via Darjeeling to Jorethang. Shared jeeps run from Siliguri to Jorethang and from Jorethang to Rinchenpong and Kaluk, with a few direct jeeps in the mornings.

faqs.a: Neither is better; they suit different travellers. Rinchenpong is best for walkers, with the old monastery, Resum Gompa and Poison Lake reachable on foot. Kaluk has more village resorts on the motor road, bigger rooms and less climbing, which suits families and older travellers. They are only about 3 km apart, so you can easily see both from either base.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: Two nights is ideal. That gives you one full day for the monastery, the forest walk to Resum Gompa and a wander over to Kaluk, plus two chances at a clear Kangchenjunga sunrise. Add a third night for a day trip to Hilley and the Barsey rhododendron walk, which takes about 2–2.5 hours each way by car.

faqs.q: How far is Rinchenpong from Pelling?
faqs.a: About 35–40 km, or 1.5–2 hours by car on winding hill roads. Many travellers combine the two: two nights in Pelling for Pemayangtse, Rabdentse and Khecheopalri Lake, then two nights in Rinchenpong or Kaluk for the quiet and the view. Shared jeeps between the two are irregular, so a reserved car is the easiest way.

faqs.q: Can you see Kangchenjunga from Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: Yes. The whole Kangchenjunga range, including Kabru, Rathong and Pandim, is visible across the valleys from most of the ridge on clear days. Mornings from October to March are most reliable. In April and May haze often softens the view, and from June to September cloud hides the peaks most days.

Wikipedia dates Rinchenpong Monastery to 1730 and names Ngadakpa Lama as its founder, which would make it one of the older monasteries in Sikkim. Some other accounts give earlier dates, so treat the exact year with care. It is known for an unusual Ati Buddha (primordial Buddha) image in the yab-yum posture. Entry is free; a small donation is customary.

faqs.q: What is the Poison Lake at Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: Bikh Pokhari, or Poison Lake, is a small pond below Rinchenpong. As told locally and repeated on Wikipedia, defenders poisoned its water during a fight with British forces in the 19th century to halt their advance. Written evidence is thin, so it is best treated as a village story. The pond itself is a short walk and is quiet and shaded.

faqs.q: Which is the best hotel in Rinchenpong?
faqs.a: For character, Yangsum Heritage Farm, an old farmhouse in its own fields, is the ridge's most distinctive stay. For a resort with a garden and mountain-facing rooms, look at Kaluk options such as Mandarin Village Resort or Pine Village Retreat. On a budget, family homestays with meals are the best value. Prices are indicative; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Rinchenpong good for a family trip?
faqs.a: Yes, especially if you stay in Kaluk, where resorts sit on the motor road and need little climbing. Children usually enjoy the monastery, the orchards and the short forest walks, and the altitude of about 1,700 m causes no problems for most people. Evenings are quiet, so bring games or books. It pairs well with Pelling for a 4–5 night trip.

faqs.q: How do I reach Rinchenpong from NJP by shared jeep?
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from Siliguri to Jorethang, about 3–3.5 hours, then a local jeep to Rinchenpong or Kaluk, about 40 km and 2 hours. A few direct jeeps run from Siliguri in the mornings. Expect roughly ₹400–600 a seat in total. In the monsoon, landslides on NH10 can force a longer route via Darjeeling, so check current status before you travel.
